- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.3) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next period.
- After sharp price spikes (≥5% from prior peak), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +3% above recent high for 3–5 days.
- If sentiment turns negative (≤-0.2) and price is rising, model underestimates; add 1–1.5% to forecast to account for sentiment-driven volatility.
- Model frequently underestimates mean reversion in 30-day horizon; if 18-day history shows strong trend, adjust forecast to align with 30-day mean of prior 30 days.
- When sentiment is neutral or mixed (±0.1–0.2), model often lags 1–2 days; shift forecast 1–2 days ahead by +0.5–1.0% to capture sentiment momentum.
- If sentiment history shows repeated short-term reversals (e.g., +0.5 → -0.3 → +0.2), model fails to adjust; apply smoothing filter to reduce forecast volatility by 15–20%.
